records.notes: The visible lexical form is consistent; Warsh shows اٰتَيۡتَنَا while the other editions show ءَاتَيۡتَنَا, an initial alif/hamza presentation difference.
Visible forms show شُرَكَآءَ in Hafs/Bazzi/Duri/Qunbul/Susi and شِرۡكٗا or شِرۡكاٗ in Shu'bah/Warsh/Qalun, a clear lexical and consonantal difference.
The visible lexical form is consistent; the forms differ in special alif/ya and hamza presentation around وَلِيِّيَ, without a confident separate lexical subtype.
The visible lexical form القرآن is preserved; editions differ in hamza, alif, and sukūn/vowel presentation, including ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ and ٱلۡقُرَانُ.
The visible lexical form الأدبار is preserved; editions differ in initial alif/wasla, dagger-alif, vowel, and stopping-mark presentation.
